title: Xen grant copy flaws allow a guest to read and write other domains' memory
summary: Xen grant-copy validation flaws allow a malicious guest to read and write arbitrary memory belonging to other domains, including Dom0. Xen 4.6 onward is affected; XSA-523 provides patches and reports no known mitigation.

severity.rationale: The attacker needs control of a guest, but can then cross the virtualization boundary into other guests and Dom0. This is high priority for developer or agent workloads isolated with Xen.

affected.note: XSA-523 provides branch patches, not a numbered first fixed release.

exposure: Relevant where Xen hosts untrusted guests, including developer and agent virtual machines.

params.instructions: For Xen 4.6 or later, verify the vendor build contains both XSA-523 fixes; a version number alone does not establish backport status.

remediation.details: Apply both XSA-523 patches for the applicable branch or obtain a vendor-patched build. The advisory provides patches for unstable/4.19 and 4.18/4.17 and identifies no known mitigation.
remediation.risk: Medium. Plan for a host reboot, interrupting all guests remaining on the host, unless the vendor provides an applicable live patch. Validate guests afterwards.

verification: Confirm the running hypervisor includes both fixes after the host reboot or application of a vendor-provided live patch; validate guest workloads.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
Clarified that hypervisor remediation requires planning for a host reboot and guest interruption unless an applicable vendor live patch is available; a session restart is insufficient.
